title: Teddy Hill's trombonists object; fired
summary: Older players complained he broke up the time; he argued they should hold the tempo themselves and was fired from the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Oh, all the time. So Teddy Hill -- well, it wasn't his fault, it was some of the old trombone players, said, "Kenny keeps breaking up the time. Why doesn't he keep four beats on the bass drum?" So then I began to argue with them about the fact that if you are playing the tempo should be in your head, don't depend on me. Depend on yourself, because if you're playing music, the tempo that you're playing in is in your head. It's in your mind, or either it's no use of your being here, if you're depending on somebody to keep the tempo for you. You keep your tempo yourself. Because you can play the music without anything, alone. You can play your part.
Yeah, but you're asking more of them than --
That's what happened. So then they --
That's -- well you used to give them that framework, and they're not having it anymore.
No. So I was fired out of the band.
